final_text: On 31 October 2008 a link to Satoshi Nakamoto's paper 'Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System' was posted to a cryptography mailing list.
source_note: History of bitcoin, whitepaper posted 31 October 2008

final_text: The genesis block, mined 3 January 2009, carries a newspaper headline in its code: 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks'.
source_note: Bitcoin Wiki genesis block page, embedded text quoted

final_text: The genesis block paid a 50 BTC reward that can never be spent, a quirk of how the block is written into the code; whether deliberate or accidental is unknown.
source_note: Bitcoin Wiki: genesis reward unspendable, intent unknown

final_text: The first bitcoin transaction, on 12 January 2009 in block 170, sent 10 bitcoins from Satoshi Nakamoto to the cryptographer Hal Finney.
source_note: History of bitcoin, block 170 first transaction

final_text: The first known bitcoin price, posted by NewLibertyStandard on 5 October 2009, was $1 = 1,309.03 BTC, derived from the cost of the electricity a computer burned mining them.
source_note: BullionStar history of early exchanges, NLS formula quoted

final_text: The first recorded bitcoin-for-dollars trade: on 12 October 2009 early developer Martti Malmi sold 5,050 BTC to NewLibertyStandard for $5.02, paid via PayPal.
source_note: BullionStar: first trade 5,050 BTC for $5.02

final_text: On 18 May 2010 Laszlo Hanyecz offered 10,000 bitcoins for 'a couple of pizzas'; on 22 May he reported the trade done. The coins were then worth around $41.
source_note: Original BitcoinTalk pizza thread; value per Wikipedia history

final_text: On 15 August 2010 block 74638 held a transaction that conjured about 184.467 billion bitcoins from an overflow bug; a patched client within hours erased it from the chain.
source_note: Bitcoin Wiki value overflow incident, block 74638

final_text: Mt. Gox stood for 'Magic: The Gathering Online eXchange'; Jed McCaleb bought the domain in 2007, relaunched it as a bitcoin exchange on 18 July 2010, sold it to Mark Karpeles in March 2011.
source_note: Wikipedia Mt. Gox: name origin, launch, sale

final_text: Mt. Gox, once handling over 70% of bitcoin trades, halted withdrawals 7 Feb 2014 and filed for bankruptcy 28 Feb, reporting about 850,000 BTC lost; 199,999.99 BTC turned up in an old wallet.
source_note: Wikipedia Mt. Gox: halt, bankruptcy, lost and found coins

final_text: QuadrigaCX founder Gerald Cotten died in Jaipur, India on 9 December 2018; about C$250 million in crypto and cash was owed to some 115,000 customers.
source_note: Wikipedia QuadrigaCX: death, amount owed, customers

final_text: In June 2020 Ontario's securities regulator called QuadrigaCX 'a fraud and a Ponzi scheme': Cotten traded against clients from alias accounts credited with fictitious balances.
source_note: Wikipedia QuadrigaCX quoting OSC June 2020 report

final_text: FTX's fall began with a CoinDesk report on 2 Nov 2022 that 40% of Alameda's $14.6 billion in assets was FTX's own FTT token; about $6 billion was withdrawn within 72 hours.
source_note: Wikipedia Bankruptcy of FTX: CoinDesk report, withdrawals

final_text: FTX and over 100 affiliates filed Chapter 11 on 11 Nov 2022; the new CEO, who had handled Enron, said he had never seen 'such a complete failure of corporate controls'.
source_note: Wikipedia Bankruptcy of FTX: filing date, John J. Ray quote

final_text: From 9 May 2022 the 'algorithmic stablecoin' UST broke its dollar peg and fell to about 10 cents within a week, erasing almost $45 billion of Terra market value.
source_note: Wikipedia Terra; SEC press release 2023-32 on depeg

final_text: In August 2016 hackers took 119,756 bitcoins, about $72 million then, from Bitfinex; customers took a 36% haircut, and coins worth $3.6 billion were seized in 2022.
source_note: Wikipedia 2016 Bitfinex hack: amount, haircut, seizure

final_text: Economist Robert Shiller proposed perpetual futures in 1992 for illiquid assets; the crypto inverse perpetual was first built for the ICBIT exchange in 2011.
source_note: Wikipedia Perpetual futures: Shiller 1992, ICBIT 2011

final_text: BitMEX launched its XBTUSD perpetual swap on 13 May 2016, a bitcoin-dollar future with no expiry; perpetuals now carry over 75% of crypto derivatives volume.
source_note: DiarioBitcoin: XBTUSD launch date, perpetuals' volume share

final_text: Perpetuals are tethered to spot by funding: on Binance every 8 hours (00:00, 08:00, 16:00 UTC) longs pay shorts when the rate is positive, trader to trader, no house fee.
source_note: Binance FAQ on funding rates and times

final_text: Every 210,000 blocks the miner reward halves: 50 to 25 BTC on 28 Nov 2012, to 12.5 on 9 July 2016, to 6.25 on 11 May 2020.
source_note: Kraken halving history; Bitcoin Wiki for 210,000 blocks

final_text: The fourth halving came at block 840,000 on 20 April 2024, about 00:09 UTC, cutting the reward for each new block to 3.125 bitcoins.
source_note: Wikipedia Bitcoin halving; Kraken confirms 00:09 UTC

final_text: Bitcoin's supply stops just short of 21 million, about 20,999,999.98 BTC; at constant mining power the last fraction would be mined around 7 May 2140.
source_note: Bitcoin Wiki controlled supply, cap and 2140 estimate

final_text: On 10-11 Oct 2025, after a tariff threat against China, a liquidation cascade forced out 1,618,240 traders and $19.13 billion of positions in 24 hours, a record per CoinGlass.
source_note: Decrypt quoting CoinGlass liquidation data

final_text: On 17 Sept 2015, in an order against Coinflip over unregistered bitcoin options, the CFTC held for the first time that bitcoin and other virtual currencies are commodities.
source_note: CFTC press release 7231-15, Coinflip order

final_text: Cboe listed the first US bitcoin futures, ticker XBT, one bitcoin per contract, on 10 Dec 2017; CME followed on 17 Dec 2017 with ticker BTC, five bitcoins per contract.
source_note: FXStreet on Cboe and CME contract specs and dates

final_text: The day CME futures opened, 17 Dec 2017, bitcoin briefly hit $19,783.06, a peak; by September 2018 cryptocurrencies had fallen 80% from their January 2018 highs.
source_note: Wikipedia Cryptocurrency bubble timeline

final_text: On 10 Jan 2024 the SEC approved US spot bitcoin ETPs after losing the Grayscale case; Chair Gensler added: 'we did not approve or endorse bitcoin'.
source_note: SEC Chair Gensler statement, 10 January 2024

final_text: El Salvador's assembly passed the Bitcoin Law on 9 June 2021 by 62 of 84 votes; bitcoin became legal tender on 7 Sept 2021, with $30 in bitcoin offered to Chivo wallet users.
source_note: Wikipedia Bitcoin in El Salvador: vote, dates, Chivo

final_text: Under a $1.4 billion IMF deal, El Salvador amended its Bitcoin Law in February 2025, ending mandatory acceptance; bitcoin's legal-tender status lasted about three and a half years.
source_note: Wikipedia Bitcoin in El Salvador: IMF deal, 2025 amendment

final_text: MicroStrategy's first treasury buy, on 11 Aug 2020, was 21,454 bitcoins for $250 million including fees; by 14 Sept it held 38,250 bitcoins bought for $425 million.
source_note: MicroStrategy Form 8-K filed with SEC, September 2020

final_text: HODL began as a typo: on 18 Dec 2013, as bitcoin fell, BitcoinTalk user GameKyuubi posted 'I AM HODLING', admitting he had typed the title twice and it was still wrong.
source_note: Original BitcoinTalk thread 'I AM HODLING'

final_text: Ethereum's 2014 token sale raised about 31,000 bitcoin; its network went live as 'Frontier', a barebones release for developers, at 15:26:13 UTC on 30 July 2015.
source_note: ethereum.org forks timeline; ICO figure from Wikipedia ICO

final_text: The DAO, a fund run by code, opened a 28-day crowdsale on 30 April 2016 and passed $100 million by 15 May; 11.5 million Ether was committed to it.
source_note: Wikipedia The DAO: crowdsale dates and totals

final_text: On 17 June 2016 an attacker drained 3.6 million Ether, about a third of The DAO, worth about $50 million; a hard fork at block 1,920,000 on 20 July 2016 reversed it.
source_note: ethereum.org DAO fork; Wikipedia The DAO for attack date

final_text: Not everyone accepted the DAO rescue fork: users kept running the original, unaltered chain, which became a separate currency, Ethereum Classic.
source_note: Wikipedia The DAO, hard fork and Ethereum Classic

final_text: On 25 July 2017 the SEC's report on The DAO concluded that its tokens were securities and therefore subject to the federal securities laws.
source_note: SEC press release 2017-131, DAO Report

final_text: ICO mania peaked in 2017: China banned domestic ICOs on 4 Sept 2017, and Block.one later paid a $24 million SEC penalty over its $4 billion unregistered EOS sale.
source_note: Wikipedia Initial coin offering: China ban, Block.one

final_text: The Merge moved Ethereum from mining to staking at 06:42:42 UTC on 15 Sept 2022, block 15,537,394, its biggest upgrade since launch.
source_note: ethereum.org forks timeline, Paris (The Merge)

final_text: Beeple's 'Everydays: the First 5000 Days', a collage of daily images begun 1 May 2007, sold at Christie's in March 2021 for $69.3 million, paid in 42,329 Ether.
source_note: Wikipedia Everydays: price, Ether payment, start date

final_text: Larva Labs released the 10,000 CryptoPunks in June 2017 free to anyone with an Ethereum wallet who paid the fee; only 9 are Aliens and 24 Apes.
source_note: Wikipedia CryptoPunks: launch, free claim, trait counts

final_text: In May 2021 Christie's sold nine CryptoPunks consigned by their creators, Larva Labs, for $16.9 million, its first big NFT sale after the Beeple.
source_note: Decrypt report on Christie's CryptoPunks sale

final_text: CryptoPunk 7523, one of nine Aliens and the only one wearing a mask, sold at Sotheby's 'Natively Digital' sale on 10 June 2021 for about $11.8 million, a record for a single Punk.
source_note: Sotheby's press release; catalogue confirms mask and date

final_text: Kevin McCoy's 'Quantum', minted on the Namecoin blockchain in May 2014 and first sold for $4, was billed by Sotheby's as the first NFT and fetched $1.47 million there in June 2021.
source_note: Al Jazeera on Sotheby's sale; Wikipedia NFT for $4

final_text: Only 24 of the 10,000 CryptoPunks were issued as signed paper prints; each came in a wax-sealed envelope holding a 'paper wallet' key to the token.
source_note: Sotheby's press release 'Punks on Paper', 2021

final_text: In December 2025 MoMA put eight CryptoPunks and eight Chromie Squiggles into its permanent collection, all donated, in its Media and Performance department.
source_note: The Block, 21 December 2025, MoMA acquisition
